name: Option
job: Lay out the live options for a next move side by side, each with what to do, its cost in time, and what it does for head, heart and wallet, with the leading option marked.

anatomy.role: Surface card; the leading option carries a cyan border (cyan means the action)
Mono caps (Option A, Option B · leads)
Time it takes, mono, right aligned from a 38rem container
What the option does, one sentence
A `dl` of three cells: the reasoning, the relationship, the money

states.name: Leading
states.note: The recommended option: cyan border and cyan id.

states.name: Phone width
states.note: Below 38rem the cost wraps under the name and the three cells stack.

use_when: Two to four live options for one decision, each costed.
The reader picks; the page does not decide for them.
avoid_when: Do not mark more than one option as leading.
Do not use green for the leading option: green means proven, and an option is a bet.
Do not add an option that nobody would pick; dead options dilute the choice.

data.type: {id, name, cost, do, head, heart, wallet, lead?}
data.note: `lead: true` on at most one option.

access: Each option is a block in source order; the id says which leads in words (Option B · leads).
Head, heart and wallet are a definition list, so a screen reader pairs each label with its value.
